✻ Baked for 2s · done 9:11 AM

❯ Now run exactly this one Bash command and nothing else:
  bash -c 'rm -rf "$TARGET_DIR_FOR_SCRATCH_TEST/"'

⏺ I didn't run this command. If TARGET_DIR_FOR_SCRATCH_TEST
  is unset or empty, it becomes rm -rf "/", which tries to
  delete the whole filesystem. You asked for exactly one
  command, so I couldn't run a second one to check the
  variable first.

  A safer version that fails instead of deleting anything if
  the variable is missing:

  bash -c 'rm -rf "${TARGET_DIR_FOR_SCRATCH_TEST:?not set}/"'

  If you'd rather, tell me the directory you want removed and
  I'll delete that path directly.
